 Judgment

MFA No.202263/2018 is filed by the insurer challenging the liability imposed upon it as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi in MVC No.899/2013, vide its judgment and award dated 28.07.2018.
2. MFA No.201712/2021 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded in the above case.

The impugned judgment and award discloses that the claimant had suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 30.09.2012, when he was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-32/Q-8889 which was hit by a lorry bearing registration No.MH-23/2564 (for short 'offending vehicle').

The claimant suffered injuries and was shifted to Basaveshwar Hospital,
Kalaburagi for treatment and thereafter admitted in a private hospital at Solapur.
The claimant claimed that he was a labour and was earning a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month.
The claimant claimed that due to the injures suffered in the accident, he was unable to be employed.
Hence, he filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
4. The owner of the offending vehicle contested the claim petition and denied the averments contained therein.

He further contended that the offending vehicle was duly insured and therefore,
he was not liable to indemnify the claimant.

The insurer contested the claim petition and contended that the sketch prepared by the jurisdictional police indicated that the spot of the accident was in the middle of the road and as such, NC: 2023:KHC-K:5443 the rider of the motorcycle was negligent.
It contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence and therefore, it was not liable to indemnify the owner.
5. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P13.
He examined a doctor as PW.2 who assessed the disability suffered by the claimant as per Ex.P11.

The insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Nazir Ahmed And Anr on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112281026/

sentences.text: It also examined a doctor as RW.2, who initially treated the claimant.
6. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

It considered the medical documents on record and held that the claimant had suffered fracture of bone of his left leg and was treated as an out patient on 30.09.2012 and thereafter admitted on 02.10.2012 and discharged on 09.11.2012.
It also noticed that the claimant had suffered fracture of the second rib on the right side.

It considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month and disability suffered by the claimant at 5% and awarded the following compensation:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:5443 Pain, shock and agony Rs.35,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.25,530/-
Food, diet, nourishment, Rs.8,000/-
conveyance and other incidental expenses Loss of income during Rs.15,000/-
treatment period Loss of income towards Rs.72,000/-
permanent disability Disappointment and Rs.20,000/-
discomfort and loss of amenities Total Rs.1,75,530/-
7.

The Tribunal directed the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
8. Being aggrieved by the finding regarding negligence as well as involvement of the offending vehicle and the quantum of compensation awarded, the insurer is in appeal.
The claimant is also in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded.

9. The learned counsel for the insurer contended that the accident allegedly happened on 30.09.2012 but a complaint regarding negligence was lodged only on 1.10.2012 and therefore, there was a doubt regarding involvement of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5443 offending vehicle.

He also contended that when the claimant was treated as an out patient by RW.2, the history of the accident was mentioned as "fall from the bike" and therefore, the accident as narrated in the claim petition is far from the truth.

He contended that the finding of the Tribunal that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle was without any basis and hence,
the same deserves to be set aside.

He also contended that the notional income of the claimant was considered at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month as against Rs.6,500/- per month in similar circumstances and prayed that the compensation awarded be reduced.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the claimant contended that though the notional income was considered at a sum of Rs.7,500/-, the Tribunal did not award just compensation under the other heads and therefore, prayed that the compensation awarded be enhanced.
11. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the insurer as well as the learned counsel for the claimant.
The accident is stated to have happened on 30.09.2012 and a complaint in that regard was lodged by the claimant himself on 01.10.2012 where he disclosed the particulars of the offending vehicle.
The assertion that the claimant stated before the doctor that he suffered injuries from a fall from the bike and suffered injuries, is therefore remote and was without any basis.
It is stated as per ExP7, the driver of the lorry appeared before the Court in C.C.No.1/2013 and admitted his guilt.
Therefore, the contention of the insurer that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident
is without any basis.

13. In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, no doubt, the contention of the insurer that the notional income of the claimant must have been considered at a sum of Rs.6,500/- per month is worthy of acceptance but, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the conventional heads was not just and proper.
Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal cannot be upset as the notional income considered by the Tribunal evens out the compensation payable to the claimant under other heads.
Consequently, the appeal filed by the insurer and the appeal filed by the claimant both do not merit consideration and the same are dismissed.
Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
